text:
elaine: Heads-up — flaky Node SDK streaming through our proxy. After a client reconnect some chunks arrive out of order.
sam: steps to repro?
elaine: Start a long SSE stream (~2k+ tokens), kill the client (SIGINT), reconnect immediately. Node client emits later chunks before earlier ones. Seems like the parser replays buffered bits.
kyle: do we have proxy/runtime logs?
elaine: pasted minimal logs below. Note seq numbers:
```
[proxy] 2026-03-18T14:01:23Z conn=42 client=10.2.3.4 stream-id=abc start
[proxy] 2026-03-18T14:01:25Z conn=42 client disconnected (tcp reset)
[proxy] 2026-03-18T14:01:25Z conn=43 client=10.2.3.4 reconnect stream-id=abc resume=false
[runtime] 2026-03-18T14:01:26Z output chunk seq=5 id=abc
[runtime] 2026-03-18T14:01:27Z output chunk seq=3 id=abc
```
elaine: runtime's seqs are non-monotonic after reconnect when observed from proxy.
sam: Is this Node-specific? Python SDK ok?
elaine: In our tests Python iterator client keeps order. Node uses `sse-parser v1.3` which appears to mix buffered leftover data with new frames and yields them according to parser internals.
kyle: So two hypotheses: (A) proxy/runtime replays old buffers on handoff or (B) Node parser doesn't preserve server-provided ordering metadata. Which did the tcp dump show?
elaine: I dumped raw TCP. Server emitted seq=3,4,5 in order. Proxy delivered 5 then 3. So server order is correct — proxy is stitching streams badly.
sam: Any auth or token refresh happening during reconnect? Maybe a refresh middleware opens a second backend connection and we accidentally merge flows.
elaine: Yes — our NewAuth middleware triggers a backend handshake when token expired mid-stream. That briefly forks the stream while the original connection is still being drained. That matches the interleaving.
kyle: Token refresh should never create a secondary active backend for the same client stream without a resume protocol.
elaine: Short-term mitigations I propose:
- SDKs: debounce reconnect attempts (Node: 200ms) and only allow one reconnect in-flight per stream id.
- Proxy/runtime: add `X-Stream-Seq` and `X-Resume-Token` headers on chunks and initial handshake.
- Long-term: implement resume protocol: client `?resume_after=<seq>` to request continuation after a given seq.
sam: For Node SDK we can implement a safe reconnect wrapper, e.g.:
```
let reconnecting = false;
ws.on('close', () => {
  if (reconnecting) return;
  reconnecting = true;
  setTimeout(() => { reconnect(); reconnecting=false }, 200);
});
```
sam: Also document that mid-stream token refresh is unsupported by default; SDKs should either refresh proactively or fail the stream and let app resume.
kyle: Add tests: devex/samples should include forced token expiry and assert no chunk reordering.
devx-bot: Reminder: file a bug ticket with logs and minimal repro.
elaine: Filed ENG-STREAM-1122 with logs and a small tcp dump. cc @kyle @sam
sam: Another subtlety — SSE event boundaries matter. If proxy splits inside an `event:` or `data:` line and reattaches later, naive parsers may emit partial events. Ensure we never cut inside a line.
kyle: Good point. Also include `seq` inside the JSON payload in `data:` as last-resort ordering guard, e.g.:
```
data: {"seq": 42, "delta": "..."}

```
That lets clients reorder safely on receipt.
elaine: I'll replace `sse-parser` in Node SDK with a tiny state-machine that waits for a full event (double newline) before emitting. That should stop mid-event emissions.
sam: Python SDK: add `resume_after` param to `client.stream(resume_after=...)` and auto-attempt resume if server returns `X-Resume-Token`.
elaine: Question for the team — should reconnect during an active stream be fatal by default? If fatal, apps get a deterministic error and can retry with a fresh prompt.
kyle: Default to resilient: try a single resume, then surface an explicit error. Provide `fail_fast=True` opt-in.
sam: Also update onboarding docs: streaming token TTL should be >= expected stream duration and include examples for refresh patterns.
elaine: I'll open a Node PR with the debounce + parser change and add a sample in `devex/samples/streaming-resume` showing reconnect/resume flows. Pushing PR now.
elaine: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-node/pull/489
sam: Can infra run a quick audit on proxy handoff to ensure we don't interleave buffers on connection handoff?
infra-bot: Scheduled: Proxy handoff audit (INFRA-731) — ETA 2026-03-19 10:00 UTC.
kyle: Thanks. Let's track ENG-STREAM-1122 + INFRA-731 + sdk-node PR 489 + python resume PR.
elaine: :thumbsup:
sam: Closing loop — if infra confirms proxy is at fault we may block the patch release; otherwise ship SDK mitigations first.
